content.summary: (Reuters) -Financial software maker OneStream is exploring strategic options including a possible sale, less than 18 months after its ​stock market debut, according to three people familiar with the matter. content.title: BMW boosts profit margin, Toyota raises outlook
content.summary:
STORY: BMW's core profit margin rose in the third quarter.

The German automaker beat forecasts on Wednesday (November 5) with an operating margin of 5.2% for its automotive unit in the July to September period.

That was up from 2.3% a year earlier.

Group earnings before interest and tax met forecasts at $2.7 billion, while revenues were slightly weaker than expected.

BMW's results were a bright spot in another difficult quarter for Europe's carmakers, who have endured high U.S. tariffs and cheap Chinese rivals.

BMW cut its full-year guidance last month due to tariff costs and slow growth in China.

The group said it still expected the margin for cars within a range of 5% to 6%, slipping from 6.3% last year.

Wednesday's update comes as the auto giant passed the peak in research and development spending on a new all-electric range.

It expects the first model from the "Neue Klasse" series to drive growth next year.

Elsewhere, Japanese rival Toyota raised its full-year profit forecast Wednesday.

The automaker bet solid performance outside the U.S. would help it ride out the impact of President Donald Trump's tariffs.

The world's top-selling carmaker now expects operating profit of $22.6 billion for the financial year to the end of March.

That's up 6% from the $20.7 billion it previously forecast.

However, operating profit fell 27% to $5.4 billion in the most recent quarter - short of analyst projections.

It was Toyota's second straight decline in quarterly profits.

Shares in BMW were up around 4%, while Toyota fell just over 3.6%.
